datasets.name: BCIT Advanced Guard Duty
datasets.description: EEG dataset from the Advanced Guard Duty study, which measured sustained vigilance in a realistic setting. Participants verified replica ID badges against reference face images while the ID presentation rate and verification criteria varied across ten 5-minute blocks. Recordings include 256-channel BioSemi EEG with eye and mastoid channels, along with eye tracking and behavioral data on accuracy and processing time. The driving tasks that accompanied the guard duty task are not included.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Touryan (data and curation), Brent Lance (data), Scott Kerick (data), Anthony Ries (data), Kaleb McDowell(data), Tony Johnson (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: BCIT Auditory Cueing
datasets.description: EEG and behavioral dataset from a prolonged simulated driving study in which participants completed two 45-minute driving sessions with lateral perturbations and auditory cues. Cues were either random or predictive of perturbation onset. The study was designed to identify driver fatigue biomarkers from EEG and to compare them with objective driving performance measures. Data are in BIDS format and include EEG, eye tracking and vehicle logs.
datasets.authors: Javier Garcia (data), Justin Brooks (data), Scott Kerick (data), Tony Johnson (data and curation), Tim Mullen (data), Jean Vettel (data), Jonathan Touryan (curation), Kay Robbins (curation)

datasets.name: A synchronized multimodal neuroimaging dataset to study brain language processing
datasets.description: SMN4Lang is a synchronized multimodal neuroimaging dataset for studying brain language processing. It contains fMRI and MEG recordings from the same 12 participants listening to about 6 hours of naturalistic Mandarin Chinese stories. It also includes structural T1/T2, diffusion MRI, resting-state fMRI, and linguistic annotations of the stimuli such as word frequencies, part-of-speech tags, syntactic trees, time-aligned characters and words, and word embeddings.
datasets.authors: Shaonan Wang, Xiaohan Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Chengqing Zong

datasets.name: what_are_we_talking_about
datasets.description: EEG dataset titled 'what_are_we_talking_about', authored by Boncz, Toth, and Winkler. It is a BIDS-formatted raw EEG dataset mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds004075). The README provides little detail on the experimental paradigm.
datasets.authors: Adam Boncz, Brigitta Toth, István Winkler

datasets.name: Moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing
datasets.description: Human electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 80 participants who reported their attitudes on a set of sociopolitical issues and then viewed photographs of protests about those same issues. Each photo was preceded by a pie chart showing low, medium, or high social support for the issue. After each photo, participants rated their support for the protestors. The dataset supports investigation of how moral conviction and metacognitive ability shape multiple stages of information processing.
datasets.authors: Yoder, Keith J, Decety, Jean

datasets.name: The time-course of feature-based attention effects dissociated from temporal expectation and target-related processes
datasets.description: Human EEG recordings from 20 participants viewing rapid sequences of overlaid oriented grating pairs while detecting a target grating of a specific orientation. Feature-based attention was manipulated by cueing one of two gratings by colour, and temporal expectation was manipulated by making stimulus onset timing predictable or unpredictable. The dataset supports investigation of the time-course of attention effects dissociated from temporal expectation and target-related processes.
datasets.authors: Moerel, Denise, Grootswagers, Tijl, Robinson, Amanda, Shatek, Sophia, Woolgar, Alexandra, Carlson, Thomas, Rich, Anina

datasets.name: Trance channeling EEG study
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 13 carefully screened participants who each completed two sessions on different days. Each session alternated 5-minute blocks of trance channeling and resting state, with three periods per condition. The dataset supports investigation of neural activity during trance channeling compared with rest.
datasets.authors: Cedric Cannard, Arnaud Delorme, Helane Wahbeh
datasets.eeg_reference: Fp1 AF7 AF3 F1 F3 F5 F7 FT7 FC5 FC3 FC1 C1 C3 C5 T7 TP7 CP5 CP3 CP1 P1 P3 P5 P7 P9 PO7 PO3 O1 Iz Oz POz Pz CPz Fpz Fp2 AF8 AF4 Afz Fz F2 F4 F6 F8 FT8 FC6 FC4 FC2 FCz Cz C2 C4 C6 T8 TP8 CP6 CP4 CP2 P2 P4 P6 P8 P10 PO8 PO4 O2

datasets.name: Electrode walking study
datasets.description: Mobile EEG dataset from 18 participants performing tasks outdoors: resting eyes open/closed, an auditory oddball task while standing, walking alone, or walking with an experimenter, and walking-together conditions (natural, blinded control, synchronized). Each participant was recorded twice, once with active and once with passive electrodes, in counterbalanced order. The dataset supports comparison of electrode types and study of EEG during real-world walking and interpersonal step synchronization.
datasets.authors: Joanna Scanlon, Nadine Jacobsen, Marike Maack, Stefan Debener

datasets.name: TMS-EEG-MRI-fMRI-DWI data on paired associative stimulation and connectivity (Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, Chicago, IL)
datasets.description: Multimodal dataset from a bi-focal, MRI-navigated TMS-EEG study of cortico-cortical paired associative stimulation (ccPAS) targeting left and right primary motor cortex (M1). Pulses were delivered with inter-hemispheric asynchronies of 4, 9, or 14 ms. Single-pulse TMS-EEG and resting-state EEG were recorded before and at 10 and 60 minutes after ccPAS to assess modulation of effective connectivity. Structural T1w MRI is provided for all subjects, with resting-state fMRI and HARDI diffusion imaging for some. Additional sessions stimulated left M1 or DLPFC at various intensities.
datasets.authors: Julio Cesar Hernandez Pavon, Nils Schneider Garces, John Patrick Begnoche, Lee Miller, Tommi Raij

datasets.name: Effect of obesity on arithmetic processing in preteens with high and low math skills. An event-related potentials study
datasets.description: This dataset contains 128-channel EEG recordings from sixty-two obese and non-obese preteens performing a delayed-verification arithmetic task. It supports investigation of how obesity relates to arithmetic processing, as indexed by event-related potentials, in children with high and low math skills. Participant information includes age, gender, body mass index, and task performance.
datasets.authors: Graciela C. Alatorre-Cruz, Heather Downs, Darcy Hagood, Seth T. Sorensen, D. Keith Williams, Linda Larson-Prior

datasets.name: Embodied Learning for Literacy EEG
datasets.description: EEG recordings from children performing letter discrimination and visual search tasks involving the mirror-image letters b and d, collected in an embodied learning for literacy study. Each participant completed a pre-intervention discrimination task, an intervention-phase visual search task, and a post-intervention discrimination task. Participants were assigned to an intervention or control group, and events mark stimulus presentation of b and d letters, including practice trials.
datasets.authors: Linn Damsgaard, Marta Topor, Anne-Mette Veber Nielsen, Anne Kær Gejl, Anne Sofie Bøgh Malling,  Mark Schram Christensen, Rasmus Ahmt Hansen,  Søren Kildahl, Jacob Wienecke

datasets.name: Attended speaker paradigm (cEEGrid data)
datasets.description: This dataset pools cEEGrid ear-EEG recordings from two earlier studies, with 15 participants from Jaeger et al. (2020) and 21 from Holtze et al. (2021). Participants performed a two-competing-speaker paradigm in which they attended to either the left or right of two simultaneously presented audio books. Blocks were presented in omnidirectional or beamforming conditions, so the data can be used to study auditory attention decoding to continuous speech with ear-EEG.
datasets.authors: Bjoern Holtze, Marc Rosenkranz, Manuela Jaeger, Stefan Debener, Bojana Mirkovic

datasets.name: BRAR_NQ
datasets.description: MEG recordings from the BRAR_NQ study, which examines neural responses in the human brain to melodic recitation of the Noble Qur'an. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and was collected by the Universiti Sains Malaysia neuroscience research group as part of work on brain reward and anti-reward circuitry.
datasets.authors: Nur Syairah Ab Rani, Nurfaizatul Aisyah Ab Aziz, Mohammed Farouq Reza, Muzaimi Mustapha

datasets.name: MAVIS
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 24 healthy participants performing a multisensory (audio-visual) detection task. Participants detected targets embedded in simultaneous auditory and visual noise while selective attention varied. The dataset supports investigation of EEG spectral dynamics, including the spectral exponent, under changing attention and sensory statistics.
datasets.authors: Leonhard Waschke, Thomas Donoghue, Lorenz Fiedler, Sydney Smith, Douglas Garrett, Bradley Voytek, Jonas Obleser

datasets.name: Fribourg Ultimatum Game in Schizophrenia Study
datasets.description: This dataset contains 128-channel EEG recorded during an Ultimatum Game (UG) task in patients with psychosis episodes (n=19) and healthy controls (n=24). Participants played the game in both the responder and proposer roles. Data were collected at the University of Fribourg, Switzerland, to study social decision-making in schizophrenia.
datasets.authors: Anna Padée, Pascal Missonnier, Anne Prévot, Grégoire Favre, Isabelle Gothuey, Marco Merlo, Jonas Richiardi

datasets.name: Meditation vs thinking task
datasets.description: EEG recordings from experienced meditation practitioners performing alternating meditation and active thinking blocks. Data were collected at the Meditation Research Institute in Rishikesh, India. The design includes breath-counting and tradition-specific meditation, with a control group performing breath counting in both meditation blocks.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme, Claire Braboszcz

datasets.name: EEG: First Episode Psychosis vs. Control Resting Task 2
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from healthy controls and individuals with first episode psychosis (FEP), representing the second of two independently collected samples. The dataset includes 5-minute resting recordings acquired with a 60-channel 10-10 cap alongside an Elekta Neuromag Vectorview system, and a phenotype directory with clinical, cognitive, and socioeconomic assessments. Subjects who shared a montage with the first acquisition (Task 1) are excluded here.
datasets.authors: Dean Salisbury, Dylan Seebold, Brian Coffman

datasets.name: EEG: First Episode Psychosis vs. Control Resting Task 1
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from healthy controls and individuals with first episode psychosis (FEP), representing the first of two independently collected samples. The dataset includes 5-minute resting recordings with a 60-channel 10-10 cap, plus phenotype data covering clinical, cognitive, and socioeconomic assessments. It supports investigation of resting-state cortical abnormalities in the early schizophrenia spectrum.
datasets.authors: Dean Salisbury, Dylan Seebold, Brian Coffman

datasets.name: Multisensory Correlation Detector
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from 13 participants who viewed and heard audiovisual sequences while performing causality judgment and temporal order judgment tasks. The same six audiovisual sequences were used in both tasks, which allowed endogenous task demands to be manipulated while sensory input stayed constant. Auditory-only and visual-only localizer blocks are also included, along with anatomical MRI, EOG, ECG and empty-room recordings. The dataset supports research on multisensory correlation computations in the human brain.
datasets.authors: Pesnot Lerousseau, J., Parise, C., Ernst, MO., van Wassenhove, V.

datasets.name: Capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations: EEG data from Experiment 2
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 24 participants viewing static images of moving and non-moving, natural and artificial objects. The study tests whether capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations, separate from aliveness or animacy. Participants completed a speeded classification task and a passive rapid serial visual presentation task. The dataset includes raw BrainVision data, preprocessed derivatives, decoding results, analysis code, and 400 CC0 stimulus images.
datasets.authors: Shatek, Sophia M., Robinson, Amanda K., Grootswagers, Tijl, Carlson, Thomas A.

datasets.name: Capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations: EEG data from Experiment 1
datasets.description: EEG dataset from Experiment 1 of a study on whether capacity for movement is an organisational principle in visual object representations. Twenty-four participants viewed images of moving or non-moving, natural or artificial objects, completing a time-pressured aliveness classification task and a passive RSVP viewing task with a fixation-colour detection response. The release includes raw BrainVision EEG, preprocessed EEGLAB and CoSMoMVPA data, decoding results, analysis code, and 400 CC0 stimulus images.
datasets.authors: Shatek, Sophia M., Robinson, Amanda K., Grootswagers, Tijl, Carlson, Thomas A.

datasets.name: Epilepsy-iEEG-Interictal-Multicenter-Dataset
datasets.description: A multicenter dataset of interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from de-identified epilepsy patients, with sleep or awake state annotated where available. Data come from NIH, Johns Hopkins Hospital and University of Miami Jackson Memorial Hospital, and include patients treated with resection/ablation or responsive neurostimulation (RNS). Derivatives include source-sink connectivity analyses and high-frequency oscillation (HFO) detections using RMS and Hilbert detectors.
datasets.authors: Gunnarsdottir, Kristin, Li, Adam, Smith, Rachel, Kang, Joon, Korzeniewska, Anna, Crone, Nathan, Rouse, Adam, Cheng, Jennifer, Kinsman, Michael, Landazuri, Patrick, Uysal, Utku, Ulloa, Carol, Cameron, Nathaniel, Cajigas, Iahn, Jagid, Jonathan, Kanner, Andres, Elarjani, Turki, Bicchi, Manuel, Inati, Sara, Zaghloul, Kareem, Boerwinkle, Varina, Wyckoff, Sarah, Barot, Niravkumar, Gonzalez-Martinez, Jorge, Sarma, Sridevi

datasets.name: Dataset Clinical Epilepsy iEEG to BIDS - RESPect_longterm_iEEG
datasets.description: A clinical intracranial EEG (iEEG) dataset from 12 epilepsy surgery patients drawn from the RESPect (Registry for Epilepsy Surgery Patients) collection at the University Medical Center Utrecht. It includes six intraoperative ECoG recordings and six long-term recordings (three ECoG, three SEEG). The data are organized in BIDS, with session and run conventions that capture the surgical stage or the monitoring day and time, and the task labels describe the patient's state.
datasets.authors: van Blooijs D., Demuru M., Zweiphenning W, Hermes D., Leijten F., Zijlmans M.
datasets.bids_version: Brain Imaging Data Structure Specification v1.6.0

datasets.name: Prediction Error
datasets.description: EEG and motion-capture dataset from 19 participants performing a haptic interaction task in virtual reality, in which participants touched virtual objects while visual, vibrotactile, and electrical muscle stimulation feedback was varied. Some trials were designed as oddball conflicts to elicit prediction error responses. The recordings support research on the neural correlates of prediction errors and on detecting unrealistic interactions in cyber-physical systems.
datasets.authors: Lukas Gehrke, Sezen Akman, Albert Chen, Pedro Lopes, Klaus Gramann

datasets.name: Dataset Clinical Epilepsy iEEG to BIDS -RESPect_intraoperative_iEEG
datasets.description: Clinical intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from 12 epilepsy surgery patients at the University Medical Center Utrecht, forming part of the RESPect (Registry for Epilepsy Surgery Patients) collection. Six patients were recorded intraoperatively with acute ECoG and six had long-term monitoring (three with ECoG, three with SEEG). The data are organized in BIDS, with separate session and run conventions for intraoperative and long-term recordings.
datasets.authors: Zweiphenning W., Demuru M., van Blooijs D., Leijten F, Zijlmans M.

datasets.name: EEG, pupillometry, ECG and photoplethysmography, and behavioral data in the digit span task and rest
datasets.description: Raw 64-channel EEG, electrocardiography, photoplethysmography, pupillometry and behavioral data from 86 participants during 4 minutes of eyes-closed rest and a digit span serial recall task. Participants memorized or passively listened to auditory digit sequences of 5, 9, or 13 items. The dataset supports work on cognitive load discrimination, event-related and oscillatory dynamics during encoding and maintenance, and links between working memory, central and peripheral physiology.
datasets.authors: Yuri G. Pavlov, Dauren Kasanov, Alexandra I. Kosachenko, Alexander I. Kotyusov

datasets.name: EEG: Probabilistic Learning with Affective Feedback: Exp #1
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 college-aged participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement learning task with affective feedback. Data were collected around 2018 in the CRCL at the University of New Mexico to examine how the Reward Positivity is influenced by affective liking of feedback. Additional scripts are included to clarify stimulus triggers and support secondary analyses.
datasets.authors: Darin R. Brown, Trevor Jackson, James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: Multisensory Gamma Entrainment
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a single healthy young adult examining how auditory, visual, and combined audio-visual stimulation entrain gamma-band brain oscillations. Gamma entrainment has been proposed as a therapeutic approach for Alzheimer's disease symptoms. The session consists of three 40-second stimulation epochs, using a 40 Hz amplitude-modulated auditory tone, a 20 Hz LED flicker, and both together.
datasets.authors: Mojtaba Lahijanian, Mohammad Javad Sedghizadeh, Hamid Aghajan

datasets.name: Imagined Speech EEG dataset comparing paradigm designs (Aguilera-Rodriguez et al. 2025)
datasets.description: An EEG dataset of imagined speech from 15 healthy participants comparing traditional cue-based and gamified (Pac-Man maze) paradigms for brain-computer interfaces. It comprises 1,800 trials of four Spanish directional commands (avanzar, retroceder, derecha, izquierda), recorded at 500 Hz from 24 electrodes. The BIDS-formatted derivative supports evaluating how paradigm design affects imagined speech decoding.
datasets.authors: Edgar Aguilera-Rodriguez, Alma Cuevas-Romero, Santiago Mendoza-Franco, Jonathan Wornovitzky-Green, Eduardo Rivera-Cerros, David Villanueva-Cazares, Luis Alberto Munoz-Ubando, David Ibarra-Zarate, Luz Maria Alonso-Valerdi

datasets.name: SRM Resting-state EEG
datasets.description: This dataset contains four-minute eyes-closed resting-state EEG recordings extracted from the Stimulus-Selective Response Modulation (SRM) project paradigm at the University of Oslo. It includes 64-channel BioSemi recordings from 111 healthy control participants at a first session (t1), with a subset re-recorded at a later session (t2). Raw data are provided with a fully automated cleaned derivative, along with demographic and cognitive test scores.
datasets.authors: Christoffer Hatlestad-Hall, Trine Waage Rygvold, Stein Andersson

datasets.name: Music Listening- Genre EEG dataset (MUSIN-G)
datasets.description: This dataset contains electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from 20 Indian participants who listened to 12 songs spanning genres from Indian Classical to Goth Rock. After each song, participants rated their familiarity with and enjoyment of it on a 5-point scale. The data support research on music perception, genre, and affective responses to music.
datasets.authors: Krishna Prasad Miyapuram, Pankaj Pandey, Nashra Ahmad, Bharatesh R Shiraguppi, Esha Sharma, Prashant Lawhatre, Dhananjay Sonawane, Derek Lomas

datasets.name: Simultaneous EEG and fMRI signals during sleep from humans
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous EEG and BOLD fMRI recordings from 33 healthy participants scanned at Penn State, including resting-state and sleep sessions. EEG was acquired with a 32-channel MR-compatible system, and the data are accompanied by sleep stage scores for each 30-second epoch. It supports investigation of autonomic and neural events during transient arousal changes across sleep.
datasets.authors: Yameng Gu, Feng Han, Lucas E. Sainburg, Margeaux M. Schade, Orfeu M. Buxton, Jeff H. Duyn, Xiao Liu

datasets.name: A resource for assessing dynamic binary choices in the adult brain using EEG and mouse-tracking
datasets.description: This dataset provides high-density (128-channel) EEG and mouse-tracking data from 31 adults aged 18-33, collected in 2020. It includes resting-state recordings and task recordings from food preference choices and semantic judgments. The resource is intended for studying the dynamic decision processes underlying binary choices in the human brain.
datasets.authors: Kun Chen, Ruien Wang, Jiamin Huang, Fei Gao, Zhen Yuan, Yanyan Qi, Haiyan Wu

datasets.name: EEG: Probabilistic Learning with Affective Feedback: Exp #2
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 college-age participants performing a probabilistic reinforcement learning task with affective feedback (Experiment 2). The dataset was collected to examine how the Reward Positivity (RewP) event-related potential is sensitive to affective liking of feedback stimuli. Data were acquired circa 2019 at the University of New Mexico.
datasets.authors: Darin R. Brown, Trevor Jackson, James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: Dataset on Emotion with Naturalistic Stimuli (DENS)
datasets.description: The Dataset on Emotion with Naturalistic Stimuli (DENS) contains EEG, ECG and EMG recordings from 40 participants who were emotionally stimulated with naturalistic multimedia videos. The videos provide context for the situated conceptualization of emotions. Participants gave self-assessment ratings of valence, arousal, dominance, liking, familiarity, relevance and emotion category. The dataset also includes stimuli, code for data collection, validation and pre-processing.
datasets.authors: Sudhakar Mishra, Md. Asif, Uma Shanker Tiwary, Narayanan Srinivasan

datasets.name: APPLESEED Example Dataset
datasets.description: Longitudinal EEG recordings from 13 infants collected at 4, 8, and 12 months of age, with test-retest reliability assessed through two sessions within one week at 4 months. The complete dataset comprises 48 recording sessions, including 11 infants with all four sessions and 2 infants with reliability sessions only. It was used to develop and validate the APPLESEED automated preprocessing pipeline for estimating scale-wise entropy from pediatric EEG, and is provided as an example dataset.
datasets.authors: Cabell L. Williams, Meghan H. Puglia

datasets.name: Basis profile curve identification to understand electrical stimulation effects in human brain networks
datasets.description: This dataset contains intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from one patient undergoing single pulse electrical stimulation at the Mayo Clinic. It was collected to study the effects of electrical stimulation on human brain networks, and it supports a larger effort to build a database of single pulse stimulation data for understanding the human connectome across the lifespan. The data accompany a paper on basis profile curve identification.
datasets.authors: Dora Hermes, Gabriella Ojeda, Kai J. Miller, Multimodal Neuroimaging Laboratory at Mayo Clinic

datasets.name: Frequency Tagging of Syntactic Structure or Lexical Properties
datasets.description: A magnetoencephalography (MEG) dataset from a frequency-tagging study of syntactic structure and lexical properties in language processing. The recordings are organized in BIDS format and are intended for investigating neural tracking of linguistic structure.
datasets.authors: Evgenii Kalenkovich, Anna Shestakova, Nina Kazanina

datasets.name: Social Memory cuing
datasets.description: EEG dataset recorded while participants performed a visual working memory task in virtual reality using a head-mounted display. Memory items (a bowl, cup, plate and teapot) were cued by either a virtual avatar or a stick, with cues that were spatially valid or invalid. Participants were probed on item location and item status. The dataset includes raw and processed EEG, behavioral data, event codes and analysis code.
datasets.authors: Samantha Gregory, Hongfang Wang, Klaus Kessler

datasets.name: MEGMEM
datasets.description: MEGMEM is a magnetoencephalography (MEG) dataset of human episodic memory, released alongside a study of how neocortical alpha/beta and hippocampal theta/gamma activity contribute to memory. The dataset is organized in BIDS format and is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds003694).
datasets.authors: Benjamin J. Griffiths, María Carmen Martín-Buro, Bernhard Staresina, Simon Hanslmayr

datasets.name: EEG, ECG and pupil data from young and older adults: rest and auditory cued reaction time tasks
datasets.description: This dataset contains synchronized EEG, ECG and pupil recordings from 36 young and 39 older adults performing auditory cued reaction time tasks, plus a passive listening condition. The active tasks were a cued simple reaction time task and a cued go/no-go task, and they allow investigation of age-related differences in cortical, autonomic and pupillary responses during anticipation and perceptual decision-making.
datasets.authors: Maria J. Ribeiro, Miguel Castelo-Branco

datasets.name: Open multimodal iEEG-fMRI dataset from naturalistic stimulation with a short audiovisual film
datasets.description: An open multimodal dataset combining intracranial EEG (electrocorticography and sEEG) and fMRI recorded during naturalistic stimulation with a short audiovisual film. Recordings were collected from patients at UMC Utrecht, and the dataset supports research on brain responses to naturalistic audiovisual input and on multimodal comparison of iEEG and fMRI signals.
datasets.authors: Julia Berezutskaya, Mariska J. Vansteensel, Erik J. Aarnoutse, Zachary V. Freudenburg, Giovanni Piantoni, Mariana P. Branco, Nick F. Ramsey

datasets.name: Model-based aversive learning in humans is supported by preferential task state reactivation
datasets.description: This dataset contains raw and processed magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings from a study of model-based aversive learning in humans. The study examines how learning about aversive outcomes is supported by preferential reactivation of task states. Raw data are provided as .fif files, alongside derived processed data.
datasets.authors: Toby Wise, Yunzhe Liu, Fatima Chowdhury, Raymond J. Dolan

datasets.name: Dataset of Concurrent EEG, ECG, and Behavior with Multiple Doses of transcranial Electrical Stimulation - BIDS
datasets.description: A BIDS-formatted dataset of high-density EEG recorded concurrently with ECG, EOG, and continuous behavioral vigilance measures (compensatory tracking task) during transcranial electrical stimulation. Nine HD-tES montages targeting frontal, motor, and parietal regions with DC, 5 Hz, and 30 Hz waveforms were applied across 62 sessions with 19 participants, totaling more than 783 stimulation trials. The dataset supports study of tDCS/tACS location and frequency effects, brain state, physiology, fatigue, and cognitive performance.
datasets.authors: Nigel Gebodh, Zeinab Esmaeilpour, Abhishek Datta, Marom Bikson

datasets.name: VerbalWorkingMemory
datasets.description: Raw EEG recorded during a modified Sternberg verbal working memory task. Participants either simply retained letters or mentally manipulated them by alphabetization, at three memory loads of 5, 6, or 7 letters. Event markers label the baseline, encoding, delay, probe, and response periods for each task and load condition.
datasets.authors: Yuri G. Pavlov

datasets.name:
EEG: Electrophysiological biomarkers of behavioral dimensions 
from cross-species paradigms
datasets.description: This dataset contains human EEG recorded during three cross-species behavioral paradigms from 57 participants, collected to identify electrophysiological biomarkers of behavioral dimensions. Mouse data from the same paradigms are included in the code folder to support translational comparisons. Trigger codes were recorded as binary recombinations and can be re-translated to 0-255 values using the provided MATLAB scripts.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Greg Light, Neal Swerdlow, Jonathan Brigman, Jared Young

datasets.name: ForrestGump-MEG
datasets.description: ForrestGump-MEG is a magnetoencephalography dataset recorded from 11 participants while they watched the roughly 2-hour Chinese-dubbed audio-visual movie Forrest Gump. Data were acquired with a 275-channel CTF MEG system and are accompanied by T1-weighted anatomical MRI. Derivatives include preprocessed MEG (bad channel removal, high-pass filtering, ICA artifact removal), fMRIPrep-processed anatomical data, FreeSurfer surfaces, and MEG-MRI coregistration files. The authors acknowledge the studyforrest project (OpenNeuro ds000113) for its contribution.
datasets.authors: Xingyu Liu, Yuxuan Dai, Hailun Xie, Zonglei Zhen

datasets.name: Inner Speech
datasets.description: An open-access EEG dataset for inner speech recognition recorded from ten participants with a 136-channel acquisition system. It covers three paradigms (inner speech, pronounced speech, and visualized condition) with four command classes (Up, Down, Right, Left) across 5640 trials. It is intended to support brain-computer interface development and the study of the neural mechanisms of the inner voice.
datasets.authors: Nicolas Nieto, Victoria Peterson, Hugo Rufiner, Juan Kamienkowski, Ruben Spies

datasets.name: Runabout: A mobile EEG study of auditory oddball processing in laboratory and real-world conditions
datasets.description: Raw and pre-processed mobile EEG recordings from 44 healthy adults performing an auditory oddball task with complex tone stimuli. The task was performed in three environments of increasing complexity: a quiet laboratory, a sports field, and a university campus route. In each environment participants either counted deviant tones or ignored the tones. The dataset supports investigation of how cognitive task demands, motor demands and environmental complexity affect attentional processing, and includes the MATLAB and R analysis pipeline.
datasets.authors: Magnus Liebherr, Andrew W. Corcoran, Phillip M. Alday, Scott Coussens, Valeria Bellan, Caitlin A. Howlett, Maarten A. Immink, Mark Kohler, Matthias Schlesewsky, Ina Bornkessel-Schlesewsky

datasets.name: Childhood Sexual Abuse and problem drinking in women: Neurobehavioral mechanisms
datasets.description: This EEG dataset investigates neurobehavioral mechanisms linking childhood sexual abuse to problem drinking in women. Data were collected at Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis from monozygotic twin pairs, with twin pairs identified by a shared FamilyID. Task descriptions, subject instructions, stimulus program code and visual stimuli are provided in the stimuli folder.
datasets.authors: Ozlem Korucuoglu, Andrey P. Anokhin

datasets.name: Reward biases spontaneous neural reactivation during sleep
datasets.description: Simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset from 18 participants who played two games (a face game and a maze game) during wakefulness in a 3T MRI scanner. One game was randomly assigned to be won (reward) and the other lost (no reward). Participants then slept in the scanner with 64-channel EEG for 1-2 hours. A classifier trained on game-session data was applied to sleep-session fMRI to examine reward-biased spontaneous neural reactivation, and memory for both tasks was tested the next day.
datasets.authors: Virginie Sterpenich, Mojca KM van Schie, Maximilien Catsiyannis, Avinash Ramyead, Stephen Perrig, Hee-Deok Yang, Dimitri Van De Ville, Sophie Schwartz

datasets.name: EEG: Improvisation and Musical Structures
datasets.description: EEG recordings from musicians listening to three-chord progressions in an auditory oddball-style paradigm. Standard progressions were interspersed with exemplar deviants (different chord inversion) and function deviants (different harmonic function of the middle chord). The dataset supports investigation of how improvisational experience relates to the categorization of musical structures.
datasets.authors: Andrew Goldman, Tyreek Jackson, Paul Sajda

datasets.name: Mood induction in MDD and healthy adolescents
datasets.description: This dataset contains magnetoencephalography (MEG) and structural MRI data from adolescents with major depressive disorder and healthy controls performing a monetary gambling mood induction task (task-mmi3), along with a 10-minute resting-state scan. It supports a pre-registered analysis of the electrophysiological correlates of mood and reward dynamics. Task data are pre-processed with bad channels and segments marked, and anatomical MRIs are defaced with co-registered fiducial coordinates.
datasets.authors: Lucrezia Liuzzi, Katharine Chang, Hanna Keren, Charles Zheng, Dipta Saha, Dylan Nielson, Argyris Stringaris

datasets.name: Dataset of EEG recordings of pediatric patients with epilepsy based on the 10-20 system
datasets.description: Scalp EEG recordings from 30 children and adolescents with focal or generalized epilepsy, acquired with the 10-20 system. The first three hours of sleep EEG were recorded, and 5-minute N3 sleep intervals were extracted and bipolar referenced. An automated, clinically validated detector was used to mark high-frequency oscillations (ripples, 80-250 Hz), which are candidate non-invasive biomarkers of epileptogenicity, so that age effects on ripple rates in pediatric epilepsy can be studied.
datasets.authors: Dorottya Cserpan, Ece Boran, Richard Rosch, San Pietro Lo Biundo, Georgia Ramantani, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.name: EEG: Visual Working Memory in Acute TBI
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a visual working memory task in healthy controls and individuals with sub-acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), with mind wandering probes inserted between trials. Participants were tested across up to three sessions, from 3-14 days post-injury to roughly 4 months later, with MRI acquired only in the first session. Data were collected in 2016-2018 and have not been published in a dedicated paper.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh

datasets.name: EEG: Three-Stim Auditory Oddball and Rest in Acute and Chronic TBI
datasets.description: EEG dataset of a three-stimulus auditory oddball task and resting-state recordings from healthy controls, participants with sub-acute mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI), and participants with chronic TBI. Sub-acute mTBI and control participants were recorded across three sessions spanning roughly four to five months after injury, while chronic TBI participants completed a single session. Analysis scripts and extensive participant metadata are included to support reproduction of the associated published analyses.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Davin Quinn

datasets.name: EEG: Visual Working Memory + Cabergoline Challenge
datasets.description: EEG recordings from a double-blind, placebo-controlled pharmacological study in which healthy participants performed a visual working memory task after receiving the dopamine D2 agonist cabergoline (1.25 mg). Each of 27 participants completed two sessions, one with drug and one with placebo. The EEG data have not been previously published, while the behavioral data appeared in an earlier paper.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Michael J Frank, James Broadway

datasets.name: EEG: Simon Conflict w/ Reinforcement + Cabergoline Challenge
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a Simon conflict task with a reinforcement manipulation testing the cost of conflict. It includes healthy participants in Study 1 (n=83) and a double-blind, placebo-controlled cabergoline (1.25 mg) challenge in Study 2 (n=27), with placebo and drug sessions. Data were collected around 2012-2013 at Brown University.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Michael J Frank

datasets.name: EEG: Continuous gameplay of an 8-bit style video game
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 17 participants during continuous gameplay of Escape from Asteroid Axon, an 8-bit style video game. Participants also completed a two-stimulus visual oddball task and a two-doors gambling task. Task triggers are embedded in the EEG files and accompanied by continuous .csv logs of player movement, actions, antagonist position, and loot boxes. The data support analysis of canonical neural events during naturalistic, continuous behavior.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Joel Castellanos

datasets.name: EEG: Attended Speaker Paradigm (Own Name in Ignored Stream)
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 25 participants performing a two-competing-speaker selective attention task, in which they attended to either the left or right audio book. The participant's own name was embedded 10 times per block in the to-be-ignored stream, allowing study of attention capture and neural tracking of attended and ignored speech. Blocks alternated between an omnidirectional condition (equal loudness) and a beamforming condition (attended stream louder).
datasets.authors: Bjoern Holtze, Manuela Jaeger, Stefan Debener, Kamil Adiloglu, Bojana Mirkovic

datasets.name: EEG: Simon Conflict in Parkinson's
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a Simon conflict task with a cost-of-conflict reinforcement manipulation, recorded in 28 patients with Parkinson's disease and 28 matched healthy controls. Patients were tested twice, one week apart, ON and OFF dopaminergic medication, while controls were tested once. Accelerometer data from the most tremor-affected hand are also included, along with task code and analysis scripts.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Arun Singh, Kumar Narayanan

datasets.name: EEG: Reinforcement Learning in Parkinson's
datasets.description: EEG dataset from a reinforcement learning task performed by 28 patients with Parkinson's disease and 28 matched healthy controls. The task included volitional and instructed choices. Patients were tested twice, ON and OFF dopaminergic medication, one week apart, while controls were tested once. Accelerometer data from the most tremor-affected hand were also recorded.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh, Darin Brown

datasets.name: VEPCON: Source imaging of high-density visual evoked potentials with multi-scale brain parcellations and connectomes
datasets.description: VEPCON is a multimodal BIDS dataset with high-density EEG, structural MRI, and diffusion-weighted imaging from 20 participants. Visual evoked potentials were recorded during face versus scrambled-face discrimination and coherent versus incoherent motion discrimination. Derivatives include preprocessed single-trial EEG, FreeSurfer outputs, multi-scale brain parcellations (83 to 1015 regions), structural connectomes, and EEG source-imaging inverse solutions with code for regional time series.
datasets.authors: David Pascucci, Sebastien Tourbier, Joan Rue-Queralt, Margherita Carboni, Patric Hagmann, Gijs Plomp

datasets.name: interictal iEEG during slow-wave sleep with HFO markings
datasets.description: This dataset contains interictal intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings acquired during slow-wave sleep from 20 epilepsy patients, with annotated high-frequency oscillation (HFO) events (ripples, fast ripples, and combined events). It was converted to BIDS from the original publication's data, and the HFO markings are stored in per-run events files. The dataset has been used to validate HFO detection algorithms.
datasets.authors: Fedele T, Krayenbühl N, Hilfiker P, Adam Li, Sarnthein J.

datasets.name: Logical reasoning study
datasets.description: MEG dataset from a logical reasoning study collected by the Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience Laboratory (UPM - UCM). The dataset is organized in BIDS format and mirrored on NEMAR from the OpenNeuro deposit ds003483.
datasets.authors: Cognitive and Computational Neuroscience Laboratory (UPM - UCM)., PI: Fernando Maestu., PI: Carmen Requena, PI: Francisco Salto Alemany

datasets.name: EEG: Depression rest
datasets.description: Resting-state EEG recordings from 122 college-age participants who scored reliably high or low on the Beck Depression Inventory. Recordings include eyes-open and eyes-closed one-minute blocks, collected in two 6-minute sessions, one after EEG hook-up and one after task performance. The participants overlap with those in the probabilistic selection task dataset, and the data were collected in the Allen lab at the University of Arizona.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh  jcavanagh@unm.edu

datasets.name: EEG: Probabilistic Selection and Depression
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 122 college-age participants performing a probabilistic selection task, with participants scoring reliably high or low on the Beck Depression Inventory. Data were collected around 2008-2010 in the John J.B. Allen lab at the University of Arizona to study reward and punishment processing in depression. Analysis code to reproduce the associated publication is included.
datasets.authors: James F Cavanagh  jcavanagh@unm.edu

datasets.name: HD-EEGtask(Dataset 2)
datasets.description: High-density EEG (256 electrodes) recorded in 20 right-handed healthy volunteers in Rennes, France, across four conditions: eyes-open resting state, visual naming, auditory naming, and a working memory (picture recognition) task. The dataset supports studies of functional brain connectivity and network dynamics during cognitive tasks.
datasets.authors: Ahmad Mheich, Olivier Dufor, Sahar Yassine, Aya Kabbara, Arnaud Biraben, Fabrice Wendling, Mahmoud Hassan

datasets.name: HD-EEGtask(Dataset 1)
datasets.description: High-density EEG (256 channels) recorded from 23 healthy right-handed volunteers in Rennes, France, during visual object naming and spelling tasks. Each participant completed two conditions with two runs each, with 74 picture stimuli per run balanced for animals/objects and long/short words. The dataset supports studies of functional brain network dynamics during language and picture-naming tasks.
datasets.authors: Ahmad Mheich, Olivier Dufor, Sahar Yassine, Aya Kabbara, Arnaud Biraben, Fabrice Wendling, Mahmoud Hassan

datasets.name: NeuroSpin hMT+ Localizer DATA (MEG & aMRI)
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography and anatomical MRI recorded from 10 participants during a passive hMT+ (human visual motion area) localizer task. Participants viewed random dot clouds that either stayed incoherent or turned coherent (up or down) after 500 ms. The data come from the vision-only training group of a study on supramodal processing, visual perceptual learning, and plasticity.
datasets.authors: Nicolas Zilber, Philippe Ciuciu, Alexandre Gramfort, Leila Azizi, Virginie van Wassenhove

datasets.name: Dataset of neurons and intracranial EEG from human amygdala during aversive dynamic visual stimulation
datasets.description: Electrophysiological dataset recorded from the amygdalae of nine epilepsy patients undergoing preoperative invasive monitoring in the mesial temporal lobe. Participants viewed dynamic visual sequences of fearful faces (aversive condition) interleaved with neutral landscapes (neutral condition). The dataset provides intracranial EEG in BIDS format, together with neuronal spike times and waveforms in NIX format, enabling study of amygdalar responses to aversive stimuli from macroscopic field potentials to single-neuron firing.
datasets.authors: Tommaso Fedele, Ece Boran, Valeri Chirkov, Peter Hilfiker, Thomas Grunwald, Lennart Stieglitz, Hennric Jokeit, Johannes Sarnthein

datasets.description: An MEG dataset recorded while participants viewed colored square wave spiral gratings and the color words "blue" and "green". Eight spiral gratings (pink, blue, green, and orange, each in light and dark variants) subtended 10 degrees of visual angle, and the words appeared in white on a gray background. Each stimulus was presented for 116 ms, and event triggers identify the stimulus category. The data are suited to studying neural representations of color and color words.
datasets.authors: Katherine Hermann, Isabelle Rosenthal, Shridhar R. Singh, Dimitrios Pantazis, Bevil R. Conway

datasets.name: MNE-somato-data-bids (anonymized)
datasets.description: BIDS-formatted version of the MNE-Python somatosensory MEG example dataset (MNE-somato-data), anonymized and converted with MNE-BIDS. It includes derivatives from the FreeSurfer recon-all pipeline, MNE-generated scalp surfaces and watershed BEM, and a forward model for source analysis.
datasets.authors: Lauri Parkkonen, Stefan Appelhoff, Alexandre Gramfort, Mainak Jas, Richard Höchenberger

datasets.name: Auditory Cortex Mapping Dataset
datasets.description: A single-subject MEG and structural MRI dataset collected to demonstrate a MEG-based auditory cortex mapping technique. The participant passively listened binaurally to 1795 iso-intensity pure tones spanning 100 Hz to about 21.5 kHz in quarter-octave steps, while MEG was recorded on a CTF 275 system. The dataset also includes empty-room recordings, head shape digitization, and a 1.5T anatomical MRI processed with FreeSurfer.
datasets.authors: Jonathan Cote, Etienne de Villers-Sidani

datasets.name: PROBE iEEG
datasets.description: PROBE iEEG is an intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) dataset from six participants with pre- and post-surgery MRI, collected under the DSI-SEEG protocol. The dataset includes raw iEEG recordings across 12 runs per subject, along with events, channel, and electrode metadata. A known issue is that all signal files are identical, so the recordings should not be treated as distinct runs.
datasets.authors: Philippe DOMENECH, Sylvain RHEIMS, Etienne KOECHLIN

datasets.name: EEG data from an auditory oddball task
datasets.description: EEG recordings from an auditory oddball task collected at the Meditation Research Institute in Rishikesh, India. Participants completed three 13-minute sessions with standard tones, oddball tones and white-noise distractors, and responded to oddballs with a keypress while their eyes were closed. The dataset supports research on auditory attention and event-related potentials such as the P300.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme

datasets.name: free walking study
datasets.description: Mobile EEG dataset from 19 participants who walked two different outdoor routes, each twice, once while pressing buttons in a self-paced manner. The recordings were collected to characterize gait-related artifacts in mobile EEG during free walking.
datasets.authors: Nadine Jacobsen, Sarah Blum, Karsten Witt, Stefan Debener, Joanna Scanlon

datasets.name: Epilepsy-iEEG-Multicenter-Dataset
datasets.description: A multicenter collection of intracranial EEG (ECoG and SEEG) recordings from epilepsy patients at four clinical centers (NIH, JHH, UMMC, UMF), organized in BIDS. Recordings are snapshots around seizure events and include clinician annotations of seizure onset and offset, seizure onset zone, and resected or ablated contacts. The data support research on localizing the epileptogenic zone, including neural fragility analysis.
datasets.authors: Adam Li, Sara Inati, Kareem Zaghloul, Nathan Crone, William Anderson, Emily Johnson, Iahn Cajigas, Damian Brusko, Jonathan Jagid, Angel Claudio, Andres Kanner, Jennifer Hopp, Stephanie Chen, Jennifer Haagensen, Sridevi Sarma

datasets.name: Imagined Emotion Study
datasets.description: High-density EEG recorded from resting, eyes-closed participants who used voice-guided imagery to enter 15 distinct emotional states, including positive states such as joy and negative states such as sadness and anger. Participants pressed a button when they began to feel the target emotion and again when the feeling waned, with relaxation instructions between the imagery periods. The dataset supports research on EEG-based emotion recognition and brain state dynamics during emotion imagination.
datasets.authors: Julie Onton, Scott Makeig

datasets.name: Human MEG recordings during sequential conflict task
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) recordings acquired during a sequential conflict decision task. The data accompany a study of conflict detection, examining cortico-subthalamic coherence and the subthalamic beta-band oscillatory response, including recordings from patients. The dataset is mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds002908).
datasets.authors: Rafal Bogacz, Vladimir Litvak

datasets.name: DBS Phantom Recordings
datasets.description: MEG recordings of a CTF phantom acquired in the presence of deep brain stimulation (DBS) artefacts. The dataset supports evaluation of artefact rejection methods for MEG data contaminated by DBS. It is a subset of the data used in a study comparing the performance of DBS artefact rejection approaches.
datasets.authors: Ahmet Levent Kandemir, Vladimir Litvak, Esther Florin

datasets.name: DataSet2
datasets.description: This dataset, named DataSet2, is an EEG dataset originally deposited on OpenNeuro (ds002833) and mirrored on NEMAR. It was contributed by Mheich and colleagues. The available documentation gives no details on the experimental paradigm or participants.
datasets.authors: Ahmad Mheich, Olivier Dufor, Sahar Yassine, Aya Kabbara, Fabrice Wendling, Mahmoud Hassan

datasets.name: A Multimodal Neuroimaging Dataset to Study Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Visual Processing in Humans
datasets.description: A multimodal neuroimaging dataset (EEG, anatomical MRI and functional MRI) for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of visual processing in the human brain, as described by the dataset title. This is a NEMAR-hosted copy of OpenNeuro dataset ds002814. The associated article was under review at the time of the record. The source README is an unfilled placeholder, so further study details are not available in the dataset documentation. Contact the corresponding authors (Seyed-Mahdi Khaligh-Razavi, Fatemeh Ebrahiminia) for more information.
datasets.authors: Fatemeh Ebrahiminia, Morteza Mahdiani, Seyed-Mahdi Khaligh-Razavi

datasets.name: Human es-fMRI Resource: Concurrent deep-brain stimulation and whole-brain functional MRI
datasets.description: This dataset contains concurrent electrical stimulation and functional MRI (es-fMRI) recordings from 26 patients with medically refractory epilepsy who had intracranial electrodes implanted in cortical and subcortical sites. Selected electrode contacts were stimulated in a block design while whole-brain BOLD activity was recorded. The resource includes pre-operative and post-operative sessions, structural scans, resting-state scans, field maps, stimulation coordinates and parameters, and fMRIPrep and FreeSurfer derivatives.
datasets.authors: Thompson WH*, Nair R*, Oya H*, Esteban O, Shine JM, Petkov CI, Poldrack RA, Howard M, Adolphs R†, *equally contributing, †corresponding author

datasets.name: DataSet1
datasets.description: DataSet1 is an EEG dataset originally deposited on OpenNeuro (ds002791) and mirrored on NEMAR. It was contributed by Mheich, Dufor, Yassine, Kabbara, Wendling and Hassan. The available documentation gives no further detail on the experimental paradigm or participants.
datasets.authors: Ahmad Mheich, Olivier Dufor, Sahar Yassine, Aya Kabbara, Fabrice Wendling, Mahmoud Hassan

datasets.name: memoryreplay
datasets.description: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) dataset from a study of episodic memory retrieval, in which participants recalled episodes while neural activity was recorded. The data support analyses of rapid neural replay of episode content during successful retrieval. The dataset includes a memory phase and a localizer phase, with trigger channels marking stimulus categories and answer onsets.
datasets.authors: G. Elliott Wimmer, Yunzhe Liu, Neža Vehar, Timothy E.J. Behrens, Raymond J. Dolan

datasets.name: A dataset recording joint EEG-fMRI during affective music listening
datasets.description: Joint EEG-fMRI recordings from 21 healthy adults who listened to music stimuli chosen and generated to evoke different affective responses. Participants self-reported their felt affective states during listening. The dataset supports research on the neural correlates of emotional responses to music, including sub-cortical activity reflected in EEG.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: A dataset recorded during development of an affective brain-computer music interface: training sessions
datasets.description: EEG, galvanic skin response (GSR) and electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings from 16 healthy participants who listened to 40 s synthetically generated music clips targeting two affective states defined by valence and arousal. Data were collected over three sessions on separate days, each with four runs of 18 trials. The recordings were made to train an affective brain-computer music interface (BCMI-MIdAS) to induce target emotional states in individual users. Self-reported valence and arousal values and auxiliary variables are included.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: A dataset recorded during development of an affective brain-computer music interface: testing session
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 8 healthy adults using a real-time, online affective music brain-computer interface. The system identified each listener's emotional state and modified synthetically generated 60 s music clips on the fly to induce target affective states defined by valence and arousal. The dataset includes self-reported valence and arousal and is one of three connected datasets from the BCMI-MIdAS project.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: A dataset recorded during development of an affective brain-computer music interface: calibration session
datasets.description: EEG, galvanic skin response (GSR) and electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings from healthy adult volunteers listening to 40-s synthetic music clips designed to target specific affective states defined by valence and arousal. The data were collected to calibrate an affective brain-computer music interface that induces target emotional states through real-time modification of generated music. Each session comprised 5 runs of 18 music trials, and self-reported valence and arousal ratings are included. This is the calibration dataset of three related datasets from the BCMI-MIdAS project.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: An EEG dataset recorded during affective music listening
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 31 healthy adults who listened to 40 twelve-second film-score music clips chosen to induce a range of emotional states. The dataset includes unprocessed EEG at 1 kHz, resting-state runs, and participants' self-reported induced emotional responses. It supports investigation of the neural correlates of music-induced emotion and was collected within the BCMI-MIdAS project.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: A  dataset  recorded  during  development  of a  tempo-based  brain-computer  music  interface
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 19 healthy participants using a music-based brain-computer interface that lets users dynamically modulate music tempo through intentional control. Participants kinaesthetically imagined squeezing a ball with the right hand to increase tempo, or relaxed to decrease it. The paradigm comprised 9 runs, beginning with a calibration run of 30 trials in pairs of increase and decrease tempo trials.
datasets.authors: Ian Daly, Nicoletta Nicolaou, Duncan Williams, Faustina Hwang, Alexis Kirke, Eduardo Miranda, Slawomir J. Nasuto

datasets.name: Numbers and Letters
datasets.description: MEG dataset in which participants viewed numbers, letters, and false fonts, presented either as single items or as strings. The experiment has two runs, single-item and string presentation, with trigger codes marking each stimulus category. The dataset can be used to study visual processing of numeric versus alphabetic symbols.
datasets.authors: Sara Aurtenetxe, Nicola Molinaro, Doug Davidson, Manuel Carreiras

datasets.name: Internal attention study
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 20 participants performing an internal attention task with eyes closed. Participants followed automated verbal instructions to relax, get ready, and mentally concentrate on a target for roughly 15-second periods. The sequence of relax, get-ready, and concentrate phases was repeated 20 times per participant.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme, Dean Radin

datasets.name: Go-nogo categorization and detection task
datasets.description: EEG recordings from participants performing a rapid go/nogo visual task in which briefly flashed (20 ms) natural photographs had to be either categorized (animal vs. non-animal) or recognized (a previously learned probe image). Data were collected over two recording days, in series of 100 images with equally likely target and non-target trials. The dataset supports research on the timing of visual categorization and recognition processes and on single-trial EEG dynamics.
datasets.authors: Arnaud Delorme

datasets.name: Differential brain mechanisms of selection and maintenance of information during working memory (MEG data)
datasets.description: MEG dataset from 22 participants performing a visual working memory task in which two Gabor stimuli were presented and a retro-cue indicated which stimulus and attribute to maintain for comparison with a probe. Each participant was recorded in two MEG sessions, with a one-back control task and anatomical T1 MRI. The data support investigation of the distinct brain mechanisms of selecting and maintaining information in working memory.
datasets.authors: Romain Quentin, Jean-Remi King, Etienne Sallard, Nathan Fishman, Ryan Thompson, Ethan Buch, Leonardo Cohen

datasets.name: A multi-modal human neuroimaging dataset for data integration: simultaneous EEG and fMRI acquisition during a motor imagery neurofeedback task: XP2
datasets.description: This dataset contains simultaneous 64-channel EEG and fMRI recordings from 16 participants performing right-hand motor imagery with bimodal EEG-fMRI neurofeedback (experiment XP2). Participants were randomly assigned to receive either a mono-dimensional or a bi-dimensional feedback display. It includes raw and preprocessed EEG, BOLD fMRI, and EEG and BOLD neurofeedback scores, supporting multi-modal data integration research. It is designed to be combined with the companion XP1 dataset.
datasets.authors: Giulia Lioi, Claire Cury, Lorraine Perronnet, Marsel Mano, Elise Bannier, Anatole Lecuyer, Christian Barillot

datasets.name: A multi-modal human neuroimaging dataset for data integration: simultaneous EEG and fMRI acquisition during a motor imagery neurofeedback task: XP1
datasets.description: A multi-modal neuroimaging dataset (XP1) with simultaneous 64-channel EEG and fMRI recorded while 10 participants performed right-hand kinaesthetic motor imagery with neurofeedback. Each participant completed motor localizer, pre- and post-training motor imagery runs, and three neurofeedback runs (EEG-only, fMRI-only, and bimodal EEG-fMRI). The release includes raw and preprocessed EEG, BOLD fMRI, anatomical data, and EEG and BOLD neurofeedback scores to support multi-modal data integration.
datasets.authors: Giulia Lioi, Claire Cury, Lorraine Perronnet, Marsel Mano, Elise Bannier, Anatole Lecuyer, Christian Barillot

datasets.name: OcularLDT
datasets.description: OcularLDT is a neuroimaging dataset contributed by Brooks, Gwilliams, Gramfort, and Marantz and mirrored on NEMAR from OpenNeuro (ds002312). The name suggests a lexical decision task with ocular measurements, but the README gives no details about participants, stimuli, or recording modality.
datasets.authors: Teon L Brooks, Laura Gwilliams, Alexandre Gramfort, Alec Marantz

datasets.name: Auditory and Visual Rhythm Omission EEG
datasets.description: EEG recordings from 18 participants who separately listened to auditory rhythms and watched visual flashing rhythms. The stimulus trains contained occasional omissions, which allowed predictive neural activity to be separated from sensory-evoked activity. The dataset supports study of the predictive mechanisms of rhythm perception. Code for preprocessing, time-frequency computation, frequency band extraction and statistics is provided.
datasets.authors: Daniel C Comstock, Ramesh Balasubramaniam
